misconception_pool.misconception: Standard sunglasses provide sufficient optical protection when grinding or handling caustic shop chemicals.
misconception_pool.fact: Personal protective equipment must be chosen based on specific chemical and mechanical shop hazards.

misconception_pool.misconception: Heavy canvas or leather work gloves protect a mechanic's hands when operating spinning drill presses, lathes, or bench grinders.
misconception_pool.fact: Rotating machinery can snag glove fabric and pull fingers into the tool, so bare hands are required near spinning shop equipment.

misconception_pool.misconception: Hydraulic valves alone hold a raised tractor loader or implement safely in place while a mechanic crawls underneath for repairs.
misconception_pool.fact: Hydraulic seals and hoses can fail without warning, so rigid jack stands or mechanical cylinder stops must support raised loads.

misconception_pool.misconception: Standard prescription eyeglasses provide sufficient eye protection when grinding metal or hammering hardened pins in a farm shop.
misconception_pool.fact: Everyday lenses can shatter on impact and lack side shields, whereas ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses and face shields stop flying debris.

misconception_pool.misconception: Running a tractor engine inside a farm shop with the walk-in door cracked open vents enough exhaust to prevent carbon monoxide buildup.
misconception_pool.fact: Diesel and gasoline exhaust rapidly reaches lethal levels indoors unless routed outside through a dedicated exhaust hose or open bays.

pamphlet_excerpts: Compression Ignition Principles: Diesel cylinders compress air until extreme heat ignites atomized fuel oil.
Hydraulic Force Transfer: Incompressible hydraulic oil transmits force through high pressure lines to cylinders.
Planetary Gear Operation: Planetary gearsets multiply engine torque to rotate drive axles under load.
Fluid Reservoir Purpose: Reservoirs store excess oil while dissipating heat and releasing entrained air.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Diesel Tracing: Trace diesel fuel flow from supply tank through primary filter to injectors.
Step 2 - Pump Inspection: Locate the engine-driven hydraulic pump and identify the high pressure outlet tube.
Step 3 - Valve Operation: Shift the directional spool valve to observe fluid extension of hydraulic cylinders.
Step 4 - Gear Engagement: Select lower transmission gears to observe increased axle torque and reduced wheel speed.

misconception_pool.misconception: Glow plugs in a diesel tractor engine fire on every power stroke just like spark plugs in a gasoline engine to ignite the fuel.

misconception_pool.misconception: Hydraulic pumps generate system pressure directly regardless of whether any load or resistance is connected to the actuator.

misconception_pool.misconception: Shifting a tractor transmission into a higher road gear increases both ground speed and maximum drawbar pulling torque at the wheels.
misconception_pool.fact: Higher gears trade torque for speed, while lower reduction gears multiply engine torque at the axle to pull heavy tillage implements.

misconception_pool.misconception: Grinding a cold chisel's struck head completely flat with sharp 90-degree edges prevents the steel from mushrooming again.
misconception_pool.fact: Filing a slight bevel around the perimeter of the struck head directs hammer force inward and slows future metal mushrooming.

misconception_pool.misconception: Pumping grease into a fitting until grease overflows guarantees the joint is properly lubricated.
misconception_pool.fact: Pumping grease too rapidly or overfilling joints ruptures rubber dust seals and admits grit.

misconception_pool.misconception: Pumping grease into every sealed bearing until grease bursts out past the rubber lip seal guarantees full bearing lubrication.
misconception_pool.fact: Over-greasing a sealed bearing pops the protective rubber lip seal, allowing abrasive field dust and moisture to enter the race.

misconception_pool.misconception: Tightening a spin-on engine oil filter with a heavy metal strap wrench prevents high-pressure oil leaks around the base gasket.
misconception_pool.fact: Wrench-tightening crushes the rubber gasket and distorts the canister; oil filters should be oiled and tightened by hand to spec.

misconception_pool.misconception: Blowing compressed air from the dirty outside surface of a paper air filter toward the inside clears dust out of the pleats.
misconception_pool.fact: Air directed from the outside drives fine grit deeper into the paper pores, whereas low-pressure air must blow from inside out.

misconception_pool.misconception: Replacing a diesel fuel filter without bleeding trapped air from the lines allows the injection pump to self-prime on startup.
misconception_pool.fact: Air pockets in a diesel fuel system cause airlock and starve the injectors, so the primer pump and bleed screw must purge all air.
